name: Erdős 780: Matoušek combinatorial proof of Kneser chromatic number

problemStatement.formal: Develop Kneser graph chromatic-number infrastructure around the Lovasz-Kneser theorem and Matousek-style combinatorial/topological proofs.
problemStatement.plain: Replace ad hoc Kneser chromatic-number axioms with reusable definitions and small-case proofs while tracking the remaining topological ingredients behind the full Kneser conjecture.
whyMatters: Kneser graph chromatic numbers are a central bridge between graph coloring and topological combinatorics.
The entry converts several local placeholders into explicit Lean definitions or theorem statements.
It identifies Tucker's lemma and related topological results as the real remaining boundary.

proven: chromaticNumber is represented as a concrete sInf-based definition rather than an opaque axiom.
The Erdos-Ko-Rado ingredient is proved from the existing ErdosKoRado.Star construction.
Small Kneser graph cases such as Petersen, KG(7,3), KG(2r,r), and KG(2r+1,r) are organized as theorem targets.
The KG(7,3) chromatic-number value is corrected to 3.
open: The full Kneser conjecture still depends on deep topological ingredients.
The proof metadata records remaining axioms in Erdos780Problem.lean and a sorry in the Aristotle companion.
Future work should connect this entry to SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber and to Tucker's lemma infrastructure.
knownResults.goal: Use the cleaned Kneser graph definitions and small-case organization as a staging point for a future topological-combinatorics proof.
